One curriculum word names the standards a course must meet. Sort into Recess or Curriculum.

teachingCards.title: Thematic Rationale
teachingCards.content: 'Learning objectives', 'core subjects', and 'academic standards' all define what a school is required to deliver and how success is measured. 'Free play' and 'lunch break' both describe time deliberately left unstructured, which educators value for social development.

teachingCards.title: Word Meanings
teachingCards.content:
Lunch break: the midday pause for eating and rest
Learning objectives: what students are expected to learn
Core subjects: the essential subjects every student studies
Free play: unstructured play time
Academic standards: the required level of achievement

relatedWords: Lunch break: the midday pause for eating and rest
Learning objectives: what students are expected to learn
Core subjects: the essential subjects every student studies
Free play: unstructured play time
Academic standards: the required level of achievement
rawExtra.correctAnswer: Recess:Lunch break, Curriculum:Learning objectives, Curriculum:Core subjects, Recess:Free play, Curriculum:Academic standards

quests.instruction: Sort each word under Lecture or Discussion.
quests.definition: A monologue, a 'prepared talk', and 'note-taking' all fit a lecture, where information flows mainly in one direction. A debate and 'group dialogue' both involve exchange, where participants respond to each other rather than only listening.
quests.example: Note-taking: writing down information as it's presented | Debate: a structured exchange of opposing views | Monologue: a long speech by one person | Prepared talk: a presentation planned in advance | Group dialogue: conversation among several participants

quests.instruction: Halfway through the curriculum: picture two teaching styles side by side and sort into Lecture or Discussion.
quests.definition: 'Passive listening' and 'delivered from the podium' both describe one-way instruction, where the audience receives rather than contributes. 'Peer exchange', 'open floor', and 'Socratic questioning' all describe participatory learning, with the Socratic method using questions to draw reasoning out of students rather than telling them answers.
quests.example: Socratic questioning: drawing out reasoning through questions | Open floor: a session where anyone may speak | Peer exchange: learning through conversation with equals | Passive listening: receiving information without responding | Delivered from the podium: presented formally to an audience
quests.exampleSentence: Socratic questioning: drawing out reasoning through questions
quests.contextSentence: 'Passive listening' and 'delivered from the podium' both describe one-way instruction, where the audience receives rather than contributes. 'Peer exchange', 'open floor', and 'Socratic questioning' all describe participatory learning, with the Socratic method using questions to draw reasoning out of students rather than telling them answers.
relatedWords: Socratic questioning: drawing out reasoning through questions
Open floor: a session where anyone may speak
Peer exchange: learning through conversation with equals
Passive listening: receiving information without responding
Delivered from the podium: presented formally to an audience
quests.nativeTip: Two of these describe learning where students shape the direction of the session.
